clue.text: He's made progress in writing

parts.note: Bunyan's allegory The ... Progress is a written work whose hero makes his progress on the page

explanation.surface: Someone has got better at writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made progress in writing' sounds like improving one's handwriting, but points to Bunyan's book, The Pilgrim's Progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian, the traveller in Bunyan's allegory, is the title figure whose journey is the book's progress.

clue.text: Drives an Austin

definitions.meaning: drives as a verb means propels or energises
Austin ... is the spy hero of Mike Myers's comedy films

explanation.surface: Someone drives an Austin car.
explanation.walkthrough: An Austin is a British car make, which sets up the motoring picture; here it is the film character's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Engines propel a machine, the same as driving it; and Austin's surname in the films completes the second sense.

clue.text: Lumber importer initially wants 1000 cut trees

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words Lumber and importer
cut says a part is removed from the word before it

parts.note: to want something is to lack it
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K

explanation.surface: A timber importer wants a thousand felled trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' signals removing K, the usual crossword shorthand for a thousand; 'initially' applies to both Lumber and importer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a flowering shrub or small tree of the olive family, so the plural names several such trees.

clue.text: Possible to oppose Brexit's lies, broken with vote to leave

indicators.note: broken says the letters of Brexit's lies are smashed and rearranged
to leave says the vote's letter must go from the mix

parts.note: a cross, X, is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A political claim that Brexit's lies were exposed once a vote went the Leave way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges BREXITSLIES; 'to leave' takes out X (a vote, the cross on a ballot), and the remaining ten letters give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be resisted is capable of being opposed or withstood.

clue.text: Mother's on the road north from southern Kenya

parts.note: mother is MA, and the 's adds S
the A1 is the great road north from London to Edinburgh, written with I for 1

explanation.surface: A mother heads north on the road from the south of Kenya.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road north out of London; crosswords write its 1 as I. 'on' places MAS above it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a pastoral people living in southern Kenya and northern Tanzania, so the name serves as an adjective for that region.

clue.text: E.g. 2 francs left by debtors?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for francs
debtors are people who owe money, so owers

explanation.surface: Debtors leave behind a couple of francs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E.g. 2' points to the answer at 2 down, of which this is a category; the question mark flags that cross-reference definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilacs, the answer at 2 down, are blooms, so they are an example of the category named here.

clue.text: Fab iconic characters shot additional sequence

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters of Fab iconic are jumbled

explanation.surface: Images of fabulously iconic stars filmed in an extra sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' just says the letters of 'Fab iconic' are used; 'shot' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Each term of the famous number series is the sum of the two before, so it is a sequence built by addition.

clue.text: They're not even getting the chance

definitions.meaning: numbers that are not even are those such as 1, 3, 5
the probability or likelihood of something happening, as in betting

explanation.surface: Uneven competitors are given an opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers like 3 and 7 are not even, and a bookmaker's prices express the likelihood of an outcome.

clue.text: Public schoolboy gets second in foreign language

indicators.note: in says the second's letter sits inside the schoolboy

parts.note: a pupil at Eton, the famous English public (fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: A boy at an English private school gets a second-place mark in his foreign-language exam.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'public school' is an elite fee-paying one, and Eton is the best known.
explanation.definitionFit: The national tongue of Estonia, a Baltic state, is a language foreign to English speakers.

clue.text: Drifting off, flat fish has raised tail section

indicators.note: raised in a down entry lifts a chunk higher up the column, nearer the top

parts.note: a stingray is a flat-bodied fish
the closing three letters of the fish's name

explanation.surface: A dozing flatfish lifts part of its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' suits a down entry: the tail section moves up the column to sit just after the first two letters. 'flat' looks like a sleepy adjective but belongs to the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander off course, so this participle means drifting away.

clue.text: We will initially spend spring near small city

parts.note: the contraction we'll, written without its apostrophe

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word spend

explanation.surface: We will spend the spring near a small English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring near small' gives the same result another way, WELL beside S, since the city in Somerset is named after its springs and is England's smallest city.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells in Somerset, with its cathedral, is famously the smallest city in England.

clue.text: Newspaper man's recollected it: "Rosebud!"

indicators.note: re-collected, gathered again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A journalist recalls the famous last word of Citizen Kane, about a newspaper magnate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like 'remembered' but reads as re-collected: the letters of IT ROSEBUD are gathered afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy editor on a paper checks and corrects reporters' stories before printing.

clue.text: Declines items charged after break in US

indicators.note: after puts the charged items behind the break

parts.note: Americans call a school break recess
ions are atoms or molecules carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: Takings fall for goods bought on credit after an American holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'items charged' suggests shopping on credit, but means electrically charged particles.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic downturns are periods when output and trade fall off.

clue.text: Sin reported in Nevada briefly

indicators.note: reported means spoken out, so the abbreviation is said as letters

parts.note: NV is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Nevada

explanation.surface: A sin is reported in Las Vegas's state.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the letters N V sound like the word for the deadly sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Covetousness is one of the seven deadly sins of Christian teaching.

clue.text: One good drawing turns up on front of graphic novel causing mixed emotions

indicators.note: on front of places the reversed part ahead of the next piece
turns up, in a down entry, reverses the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
drawing is art
a graphic novel is a book-length comic

explanation.surface: A single good drawing on a graphic novel's cover stirs mixed feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses IGART to TRAGI, which goes in front of COMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mixing tragedy with comedy provokes both sorrow and laughter at once.

clue.text: Press blackout possibly one type of feature of the Cold War

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them
a blackout is one kind of drape for windows

explanation.surface: A news blackout in the press was one of the hallmarks of the Cold War.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press blackout' reads as media censorship; split it as press (smooth with heat) and a blackout window drape.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill's phrase for the barrier dividing Soviet-bloc Europe from the West became the defining image of the Cold War.

clue.text: Where should I put the ball for kick-off? Right there!

definitions.text: Where should I put the ball for kick-off?
definitions.meaning: a football game starts with the ball placed on the centre mark of the pitch
immediately, at that very moment and place

explanation.surface: A footballer asks where to place the ball and is told: just there.
explanation.definitionFit: The ball goes on the marked centre circle point to start play, and the idiom means instantly, at the scene.

clue.text: Doctoring tip cures rattling in the lungs

indicators.note: doctoring means tampering with, so the letters of tip cures are altered in order

explanation.surface: Medical advice on treating a rattling chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctoring' fits the medical scene, but signals rearranging TIPCURES.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackling sounds heard through a stethoscope in diseased lungs are the medical term's sense.

clue.text: Proceeds with new replacement for 4th piece of jewellery

indicators.note: replacement for 4th swaps the letter in fourth place for another

parts.note: earrings, here in the plural as they are worn

explanation.surface: Money from sale of a piece of jewellery is replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement for 4th' swaps the fourth letter, R, of EARRINGS for N (new).
explanation.definitionFit: Proceeds are the money brought in, the income or takings from work or sales.

clue.text: Little orange mostly chopped up for sharing again

indicators.note: chopped up says the letters are cut into pieces and mixed
mostly keeps all but the last letter of the word orange

explanation.surface: A small orange, mostly chopped, to be divided out once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the E of orange, leaving ORANG; 'chopped up' rearranges LITTLEORANG.
explanation.definitionFit: Allotting is distributing shares, so doing it over again means apportioning anew.

clue.text: Leader of Green party's accents

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of Green

parts.note: a rave is a party; party's read as party is gives the plural

explanation.surface: The Green Party leader's accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green party' looks like the political party; split it into G and RAVES.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave is the backward-sloping accent mark found in French, as in è.

clue.text: Prophet in Latin version's with God in spirit

indicators.note: in places the Latin words inside the spirit

parts.note: gin is a distilled spirit
Deo is Latin for with (or to) God

explanation.surface: A prophet in the Latin Bible walks with God in spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin version's with God' is the Latin phrase for 'with God', a short dative/ablative form; it splits the spirit after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gideon is a judge and deliverer of Israel in the Book of Judges, called by God as a prophet figure.

clue.text: Ache in leg by right side of knee

parts.note: pins is slang for legs

indicators.note: right side of takes the final letter of knee, reading left to right

explanation.surface: Pain in the leg by the right of the knee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ache in leg' paints a sore limb, but 'Ache' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to long or yearn for something, the same as to pine for it.

clue.text: A dog from the east I raised round stormy lochs

indicators.note: from the east, in an across entry, means read right to left
round says the grew letters enclose the stormy lochs

parts.note: to raise crops is to grow them, past tense grew

indicators.note: stormy says the letters of lochs are tossed about

explanation.surface: A dog from the east is raised beside stormy Scottish lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps GREW around OCHSL (lochs made 'stormy'), giving GROCHSLEW; I goes before it and 'from the east' reverses the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The short-legged herding breed from Wales is a type of dog.

clue.text: Security concern over Trojans leads to close of Internet Explorer

indicators.note: leads to takes the opening letters of the four words that follow
close of takes the final letter of Internet

explanation.surface: A computer security worry about Trojan viruses forces Internet Explorer to shut.
explanation.walkthrough: Internet Explorer is Microsoft's browser; here 'Explorer' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Falcon Scott led the ill-fated British expedition to the South Pole in 1912.

clue.text: Spies obtain cipher used for so long in Italy

definitions.text: used for so long in Italy

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
a cipher is a zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Secret agents get a code that has been in use a long time in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cipher' suggests spy codes, but in its old sense means nought.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian farewell is the everyday way Italians say goodbye, or so long.

clue.text: Expert in court isn't prone to disorder

indicators.note: to disorder is to throw into confusion, so the letters of isn't prone are shuffled

explanation.surface: A legal specialist who does not tend to cause chaos in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court, but is a playing court.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional player or coach of the racket game is skilled on the court.

clue.text: Male has to fight to keep love in film

indicators.note: to keep says the letters hold something inside them

parts.note: to vie is to compete or contend
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A man must battle to keep the woman he loves, as in a film plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion picture, a feature shown at the cinema.

clue.text: Decipher secrets US southerners keep

indicators.note: keep says the run of words holds the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Crack the secrets that people in the American South guard.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of 'secrets', all of 'US' and the start of 'southerners'.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out or figure out a puzzle is the informal sense of this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Attaches riding gear by Christ!

parts.note: tack is the saddle, bridle and other equipment for a horse
Christ is the Son of God

explanation.surface: Someone fixes on riding equipment and exclaims in frustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christ!' looks like an oath; it is the Son of God.
explanation.definitionFit: To add something on loosely or as an afterthought, fastening it to something else.
